'''Fred Oswald''' is an American industrial organizational psychologist who is known for his contributions to artificial intelligence ethics,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lerner |first=Michele |date=January 30, 2024 |title=Worried about AI in the workplace? You're not alone |url=https://www.apa.org/topics/healthy-workplaces/artificial-intelligence-workplace-worry |access-date=2025-02-04 |website=American Psychological Association}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Zinn |first=Joshua |date=2024-03-07 |title=As artificial intelligence grows and consumers gain access, Rice joins a federal consortium on AI safety |url=https://www.houstonpublicmedia.org/articles/shows/houston-matters/2024/03/07/480005/as-artificial-intelligence-grows-and-consumers-gain-access-rice-joins-a-federal-consortium-on-ai-safety/ |access-date=2025-02-04 |website=Houston Public Media |language=en-US}}</ref> psychometrics, workforce readiness,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Lerner |first=Michele |date=2024-01-30 |title=Worried about AI in the workplace? You’re not alone |url=https://www.apa.org/topics/healthy-workplaces/artificial-intelligence-workplace-worry |access-date=2025-09-26 |website=American Psychological Association}}</ref> and the measurement of individual differences in organizational settings.<ref>{{Cite book |url=http://www.nap.edu/catalog/18427 |title=New Directions in Assessing Performance Potential of Individuals and Groups: Workshop Summary |date=2013-09-04 |publisher=National Academies Press |isbn=978-0-309-29044-9 |location=Washington, D.C. |doi=10.17226/18427}}</ref> He is currently a professor at the [[University of California, Irvine School of Education]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Our faculty - UCI School of Education|url=https://education.uci.edu/our-faculty.html|language=en-US}}</ref> Until January, 2026, he was 
the Herbert S. Autrey Professor of Social Sciences at [[Rice University]]<ref>{{Cite web |last=Gregor |first=Lori |date=2018-07-23 |title=Best Editorial Practices Associated with Robust and Reliable Research in the Science of Organizations |url=https://warrington.ufl.edu/reliable-research-in-business/2018/07/23/best-editorial-practices-associated-with-robust-and-reliable-research-in-the-science-of-organizations/ |access-date=2025-02-04 |website=Reliable Research in Business |language=en-US}}</ref> in [[Houston|Houston, Texas]]. He is a national associate of the [[National Academies of Sciences, Engineering, and Medicine]],<ref>{{Cite journal |date=2020-03-25 |title=APS Fellow Oswald Named Chair of National Academies Board |url=https://www.psychologicalscience.org/observer/aps-fellow-oswald-named-chair-of-national-academies-i-o-board |journal=APS Observer |language=en |volume=33}}</ref> a fellow of the [[Society for Industrial and Organizational Psychology]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=July 31, 2024 |title=Advocate Spotlight: Frederick L. Oswald, PhD |url=https://www.apaservices.org/advocacy/get-involved/advocate-spotlight/frederick-oswald |access-date=2025-02-04 |website=American Psychological Association}}</ref> and the [[Association for Psychological Science]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Sleek |first=Scott |date=2018-01-31 |title=The Bias Beneath: Two Decades of Measuring Implicit Associations |url=https://www.psychologicalscience.org/observer/the-bias-beneath-two-decades-of-measuring-implicit-associations |journal=APS Observer |language=en |volume=31}}</ref> He currently serves as the editor of the journal ''[[Psychological Methods]]''.<ref>{{Cite web |last=McCaig |first=Amy |date=May 21, 2024 |title=Rice's Fred Oswald named incoming editor for Psychological Methods journal |url=https://news.rice.edu/news/2024/rices-fred-oswald-named-incoming-editor-psychological-methods-journal |access-date=2025-02-03 |website=Rice University}}</ref> In 2021, Oswald was appointed to the U.S. Department of Commerce's Artificial Intelligence Consortium.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Hsia |first=Viola |date=2024-03-19 |title=Rice joins new federal AI Safety Institute Consortium |url=https://www.ricethresher.org/article/2024/03/rice-joins-new-federal-ai-safety-institute-consortium |access-date=2025-02-05 |website=The Rice Thresher |language=en-US}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last1=Schellmann |first1=Hilke |last2=Strong |first2=Jennifer |date=2021-07-07 |title=Want a job? The AI will see you now |url=https://www.technologyreview.com/2021/07/07/1043089/podcast-want-a-job-the-ai-will-see-you-now-2/ |access-date=2025-02-05 |website=MIT Technology Review |language=en}}</ref>
